github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: The After wording moved nothing on this case: both outputs produce a single [shrink] finding that cites only the request spec as the owner of the three validation rules, never mentions the model spec, and proposes removing the system spec outright rather than keeping one browser example for the one thing only the browser proves (the form actually rendering the error list). So f1 fails identically in Before and After, and f2/f3 hold identically. The Change (anchored-task loading, structured output, behaviourChange footer, unreadable-anchor rejection) is orthogonal to this un-anchored case, which explains the flat result, but the opportunity to improve f1 was missed. To make f1 hold while keeping everything else, the shrink finding should (a) name both owners explicitly — 'owned by spec/models/ledger_import_spec.rb (the rules and messages) and spec/requests/ledger_imports_spec.rb (422, no persistence, body includes message)' — and (b) propose 'keep at most one system example asserting the rendered .errors list for one invalid input; drop the other two', so the fix retains browser-only coverage instead of deleting the system spec entirely. Wording the test-economy guidance as 'name every existing spec that already owns the rule, and keep exactly the examples that prove something no cheaper layer can' would deliver that without touching severity, trajectory, or the request/model-spec-preservation facts.
